Documentation → Tools & Studio → Examples (Plugin Studio)

Plugin Studio examples

Install working examples of every Plugin Studio piece with one click — a FortiGate policy finder built from the diagram, a NetBox IP owner script, a flow explainer with two connections, and data-store apps that work with no external system.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Examples (URL /studio/?pane=examples)

What is it?#

The Examples pane of Plugin Studio holds ready-made bundles — connections, data stores, scripts and apps that belong together — written against the answers a FortiGate 8.0 and a NetBox 4 actually give. Installing one gives you something that runs, to copy from or to extend.

What does it do?#

Example Shows Creates
FortiGate: which rule lets this traffic through? An app built only from the diagram: three API calls, two decisions, an output, and actions (save the verdict to a data store, download CSV, ask for the access as a change request). The same lookup as a script. ex-fortigate, ex-policy-lookups, ex-fortigate-policy-lookup, ex-policy-finder
NetBox: who owns this IP address? A script calling a connection, and an app whose diagram runs that script. ex-netbox, ex-netbox-ip-owner, ex-ip-owner
Explain a flow (FortiGate + NetBox) One script with two connections; keeps answering when NetBox is down. ex-traffic-explainer (script and app)
Data stores: site contacts No external system: a list field fed by a data store, a query, an upsert. Published at once. ex-site-contacts, ex-site-contact, ex-site-contact-edit
  • Install creates only what is missing. An object with the same id is never overwritten, so an example you edited survives a re-install.
  • What an example installs is a template (since 2026-10-23): it can be edited, disabled, reset and downloaded from Plugin Studio → Apps, never deleted. There is no Remove any more, and every delete — app, script, data store, connection — refuses a template and says so.
  • Connections are created without a secret and pointed at a placeholder host, so nothing reaches a device until you finish their setup.
  • The Console pane gains two examples in its Studio group: the fleet as CSV for a data store import, and every FortiGate with the base URL of a connection to it.

Requirements#

  • For the FortiGate examples: a REST API administrator on the FortiGate with a read-only profile and this SATOM node as its trusted host.
  • For the NetBox examples: a read-only NetBox API token.
  • The site-contacts example needs nothing.
  • Scripts that use a connection with a secret need the vault (see Connections).

Permissions#

studio.script_library installs and removes examples. Who can run the apps is set on each app (Settings → who may use it).

How to use#

  1. Open Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Examples and press Install on an example.
  2. Follow its To finish it list. For the FortiGate: open ex-fortigate, set the base URL to https://<FortiGate>/api/v2, authentication Bearer, paste the token, Test with /monitor/system/status.
  3. Open the app, Test it, pick its ADOMs and users, Publish.

Example#

The policy finder (ex-policy-finder), step by step:

  1. Route back to the source — GET /monitor/router/lookup?destination=<source>, keep results.entries[0].interface as srcintf (port1).
  2. Is there a route? — {{ srcintf | default('') }} not empty.
  3. Ask the FortiGate — GET /monitor/firewall/policy-lookup with srcintf, sourceip, dest, protocol (6 or 17) and destport; keep results as verdict: {"match": true, "policy_id": 1, "policy_action": "accept"} or {"match": false, "sec_default_action": "deny"}.
  4. Does a rule match? — {{ verdict.match }} true.
  5. Read the rule — GET /cmdb/firewall/policy/{{ verdict.policy_id }}, keep results[0] as rule.
  6. Verdict — a Set a variable step builds one record, e.g. 'src_addr': rule.srcaddr | map(attribute='name') | join(', ').
  7. Show the verdict as key/value; any API error goes to Fail.

The same thing as a script:

from satom_script import connection, inputs, result

fgt = connection("ex-fortigate")          # SATOM adds the token

def get(path, **params):
    r = fgt.get(path, params=params or None)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return (r.json() or {}).get("results")

src, dst = inputs["source"], inputs["destination"]
ingress = get("/monitor/router/lookup", destination=src)["entries"][0]["interface"]
lookup = get("/monitor/firewall/policy-lookup", srcintf=ingress, sourceip=src,
             dest=dst, protocol="6", destport=str(inputs["port"]))
result(lookup)

Result#

Against a FortiGate 8.0.1, a flow its first rule allows on tcp/443 answers that rule's id and name, accept, and its source, destination and service objects; the same flow on a port no rule allows answers the implicit deny.

Troubleshooting#

"no secret is stored for ex-fortigate"#

The connection has no token yet: open it, paste the token, Test.

"The FortiGate did not answer: HTTP 401"#

The token was refused, or this node is not the REST API admin's trusted host.

"… is a template … templates are not deleted"#

The object was installed by an example. Templates stay: disable the app to take it out of the menus, or reset it to empty its data.
